headline: FTAI Infrastructure agrees to sell Long Ridge Energy and Power to MARA Holdings for about $1.52bn, targeting Q3 2026 close
players: FTAI Infrastructure agreed to sell Long Ridge Energy & Power LLC and related assets to a subsidiary of MARA Holdings for approximately $1.52bn before closing adjustments. The assets include a 485 MW combined cycle gas power plant, working interests in natural gas production wells and roughly 1,600 acres along the Ohio River in southeastern Ohio. Closing is expected in the third quarter of 2026 subject to regulatory approvals and customary conditions; FIP said it will eliminate $1.16bn of Long Ridge debt and use net proceeds to repay approximately $300m of corporate debt and reinvest in freight rail and terminals. Jefferies and Lazard advised, with Skadden Arps as legal counsel.
why_it_matters: FTAI Infrastructure agreed to sell Long Ridge Energy & Power, including a 485 MW combined-cycle gas plant, to a MARA Holdings subsidiary for about $1.52bn, with closing expected in Q3 2026 subject to regulatory approvals. FIP will eliminate $1.16bn of Long Ridge debt, repay roughly $300m of corporate debt and reinvest the rest in freight rail and terminals. The buyer is a bitcoin miner pivoting to AI and data centre power.
why_you_care: You ran FTAI Infrastructure. Long Ridge agreed at about $1.52bn to a bitcoin miner pivoting to AI power, closing expected Q3 2026, the gas-to-AI thesis clearing at a price.

headline: Lightpath and CableFinder strike platform partnership to widen channel-partner distribution
players: CableFinder and Lightpath announced a platform partnership making Lightpath's fibre connectivity available to channel partners through the CableFinder quoting platform. Financial terms were not disclosed.
why_it_matters: CableFinder and Lightpath announced a platform partnership putting Lightpath's fibre into CableFinder's channel-partner quoting system; terms undisclosed. Channel distribution is a cheap way to fill capacity on fibre already built and lit, lifting utilisation without more trenching. It feeds the higher-priced enterprise revenue layer but matters far less than hyperscale and carrier contracts. Incremental rather than strategic for MSIP.
why_you_care: Lightpath sits in your portfolio now. Channel distribution lifts utilisation on fibre already built and lit, but this is incremental rather than strategic.

headline: Flexential adds fifth Atlanta-area data centre, taking metro footprint to about 800,000 sq ft and 73MW
players: Flexential is adding a fifth Atlanta-area data centre of 48,000 sq ft and 4.5MW, expected online in the first half of 2028, lifting its Atlanta footprint to roughly 800,000 sq ft and 73MW. Nationally the platform spans more than 40 data centres and 360MW online or under development across 18 markets. The company has raised approximately $1bn over the preceding 18 months, including an $800m asset-backed securities offering in November. Investors include GI Partners, GI Data Infrastructure, Hamilton Lane and MSIP.
why_it_matters: ABS is now the main funding channel for scaled colocation: the $800m issue says Flexential's lease book is stable and granular enough to securitise cheaply, which funds Atlanta, Hillsboro and Dallas at once without a big sponsor equity call. At 4.5MW this is enterprise and multi-tenant work, not hyperscale, so watch whether 2028 delivery slips as southeastern power constraints bite.
why_you_care: MSIP sits on this cap table, and the $800m ABS is how your colocation platform funds Atlanta, Hillsboro and Dallas at once without a big sponsor equity call.
